_purpose: Date-specific observances (trades + breast-cancer beats) that the Researcher and Planner check each week. October is fully owned by october-campaign.json and is never matched here. Each entry is either 'override' (forces one slot's contentType + injects the angle into that post's brief) or 'supplement' (no slot change — just adds context to the week's brief).

_rule_types.nth_weekday_of_month: { month: 1-12, weekday: 'SUN'..'SAT', n: 1-5 } — e.g. n:1, weekday:'WED', month:5 = first Wednesday in May.
_rule_types.last_weekday_of_month: { month: 1-12, weekday: 'SUN'..'SAT' } — e.g. month:5, weekday:'MON' = Memorial Day (last Monday in May).
_rule_types.fixed_date: { month: 1-12, day: 1-31 } — same calendar date every year (e.g. month:7, day:4 = July 4th). Use for holidays that don't drift year to year.
_rule_types.first_full_week_of_month: { month: 1-12 } — the first Mon-Sun week fully contained in that month.
_rule_types.monthly_day: { day: 1-28 } — fires every month on that calendar day (skipped automatically in October, see _purpose).
_rule_types.explicit_range: { start: 'YYYY-MM-DD', end: 'YYYY-MM-DD' } — hardcoded for a single year. Source-announced dates (e.g. DOL apprenticeship week) move yearly — re-verify and update before each occurrence; see 'reverify_note'.

_matched_day: getActiveEntries() annotates each entry with matchedDay (MON..SUN) — the actual day in the week the rule landed on. The planner overrides the post slot on that day (not always the week's first slot).

entries.name: Independence Day (July 4th)
entries.angle: July 4th — red/white/blue, cookouts, day off (if you're not on call). Pride-in-the-trades angle: the country runs on people who show up and fix things. Product post, not a flag-waving lecture — keep it Riley-voiced and a little funny.
entries.source: Fixed US federal holiday (July 4th) — no re-verification needed.

entries.name: Memorial Day
entries.angle: Memorial Day weekend — respectful, brief mention if it lands on a post day. Not a sales-driven holiday for this brand; keep any reference low-key.
entries.source: Fixed US federal holiday (last Monday in May) — no re-verification needed.

entries.name: Labor Day
entries.angle: Labor Day — literally the trades' day. Loud, proud, funny shoutout to the people who build/fix everything, not just a generic 'long weekend' post.
entries.source: Fixed US federal holiday (1st Monday in September) — no re-verification needed.

entries.name: Thanksgiving
entries.angle: Thanksgiving — gratitude angle. Thankful for the trades community + everyone who's supported the mission this year. Warm, not salesy.
entries.source: Fixed US federal holiday (4th Thursday in November) — no re-verification needed.

entries.name: New Year's Day
entries.angle: New Year's — fresh-start energy if it lands on a post day. Good context for a 'new year, same grind' trades angle, not generic resolutions copy.
entries.source: Fixed US federal holiday (January 1st) — no re-verification needed.

entries.name: Women in Construction Week (NAWIC)
entries.angle: NAWIC's Women in Construction Week — the one week a year the whole industry spotlights tradeswomen. Lean into pride + visibility, not just humor.
entries.source: NAWIC.org (confirmed annual: first full Mon-Sun week of March)

entries.name: National Skilled Trades Day
entries.angle: National Skilled Trades Day (first Wednesday in May) — a built-in excuse to celebrate the trades loudly. Good day for a humor or pride post, not a sales push.
entries.source: National Day Calendar (confirmed annual: first Wednesday in May)

entries.name: Mother's Day
entries.angle: Mother's Day — gift angle for the tradeswoman (or trade-mom) in someone's life. Same framing as the existing Nov-Dec gift angle in inspiration-sources.json, just earlier in the year.
entries.source: Fixed US observance (2nd Sunday of May) — no re-verification needed.

entries.name: National Apprenticeship Week
entries.angle: National Apprenticeship Week — good context for posts about earning a trade rather than student debt, or shouting out apprentices.
entries.source: U.S. Dept. of Labor (DOL moved this from November to spring starting 2026 — dates are announced fresh each year)
entries.reverify_note: DOL announces new dates annually. This entry is hardcoded for 2026 only — confirm next year's dates at apprenticeship.gov before reusing.

entries.name: Monthly self-exam reminder
entries.angle: The 1st of the month is a common, low-key reminder day for breast self-exams (used by self-exam apps like Know Your Lemons). A gentle 'hey, it's the 1st' early-detection nudge — not a hard sell, genuinely useful.
entries.source: General early-detection guidance (premenopausal self-exam timing) — Mayo Clinic / Komen.org
